About Us

Building a business around the invasive species crisis

We transform invasive species into restored land, carbon removal, and community income, starting with Kenya's invasive mesquite, creating the most cost-effective path to land restoration on the market, a triple win for carbon buyers, the planet, and local communities.

Riziki turns invasive land degradation into rural income, restored soils, and verified climate value, powered by a mobile, tech-enabled biochar unit that deploys where the problem is and puts local communities to work solving it. Community members are employed to restore agricultural and conservation land, generating verified carbon removal credits and an organic soil amendment.

The result drives impact across four areas: ecosystem restoration through invasive mesquite removal, rural livelihoods through mesquite removal and biochar production jobs, smallholder support through restored land and free agronomic guidance through the first crop season, and women's economic inclusion in communities where up to 85% of women are unemployed.

Mission

Restoring land from invasive woody species while increasing rural livelihoods.

Vision

Riziki envisions a world without invasive species, where people and planet thrive.

1/6th

Of the Earth's land is highly vulnerable

The greatest risks from invasive species fall on the developing economies and biodiversity hotspots that can least afford them.

2M ha

Overrun by mesquite in Kenya

Part of a 64-million-hectare global footprint, an area the size of France, costing Kenya's economy $2.4 billion per year.

8.9M

Kenyans live in extreme poverty

89% are in rural areas. Affected communities earn as little as $0.32 per person per day, and affected women as little as $0.06.

$2,100+

Average cost to clear one acre of land

Existing responses fall short: clearance is manual and prohibitively expensive, and government programs lack the scale and funding to make a dent.

Carbon Removal Credits

Storing carbon with verified integrity

Pyrolysis Puro.earth Verified Forward Credits

Biochar is a high-carbon material produced through the thermal decomposition of biomass in a low-oxygen environment, a process known as pyrolysis. Our feedstock is woody invasive species like mesquite, converted using our proprietary Orpheus 1 kiln so that the carbon they contain is captured and locked into the soil for centuries instead of being released back into the atmosphere.

We produce biochar to Puro.earth standards, ensuring high-quality, verified carbon sequestration. Our biochar credits provide businesses with a credible, measurable way to offset emissions while directly funding the removal of invasive species and the restoration of degraded land. We are also interested in selling forward credits to buyers looking to secure future carbon removals.

Biochar

Rebuilding soil health, one field at a time

Water Retention Microbial Activity Crop Yields

Our biochar soil amendment is produced from woody invasive species like mesquite, processed through our proprietary Orpheus 1 kiln. Applied to depleted or degraded soil, it improves water retention, boosts microbial activity, and increases crop yields, turning land that invasive species have damaged into land that supports agriculture again.

For farmers and land managers, it offers a practical way to rebuild soil health while directly supporting the removal of invasive species from the landscape.

Where We Operate

Proven in Baringo, expanding across Kenya

Operations are running in Baringo County with active land agreements across farm and conservation land. Expansion into Kajiado, Turkana, and Samburu is underway.

Active

Baringo County, Kenya

Our proof-of-concept operation, running since 2022 with 25 mobile kilns across farm and conservation land. Community land agreements with Kibogoch and Shompole conservancies, supported by a formal partnership with Baringo County Government and scientific oversight from KEFRI.
